question.problem:
If $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $\text{rank}(A-7I)=0,$ which of the following statements are true?

I. $A-7I$ is singular

II. $\text{nullity}(A-7I)=0$

III. $\lambda =7$ is an eigenvalue of $A$
question.worked_solution:
Given a $2\times 2$ matrix $M,$ we have the following by the invertible matrix theorem:

$M$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(M)={R}^{2} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(M))=2=\text{rank}(M) \\  & \text{Null}(M)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(M))=0=\text{nullity}(M)\end{aligned}$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $M$ has $2$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(M)+\text{nullity}(M)=2.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statements I is true. By the invertible matrix theorem, since $\text{nullity}(A-7I)\ne 0,$ we obtain that $A-7I$ must be singular.

- Statement II is false. According to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(A-7I) & =2-\text{rank}(A-7I) \\  & =2-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. Notice that if $M=A-7I$ is singular, then $(A-7I)x=0$ has nonzero solutions which will be eigenvectors of $A.$ As a result, $\lambda =7$ is an eigenvalue of $A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
